messages.content: Calculate the slope gradient in degree between two points on a landscape with coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437).

function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you compute the slope gradient, but I’ll need the **elevation (height above sea level)** for each of the two points.  
The slope gradient is defined as the change in elevation divided by the horizontal distance between the points:

\[
\text{slope (in degrees)} = \arctan\!\left(\frac{\Delta \text{elevation}}{\text{horizontal distance}}\right)
\]

With only latitude/longitude coordinates we can calculate the horizontal distance (using the haversine formula), but we can’t determine the vertical component without elevation data.

Could you provide the elevations for:
- Point 1: (40.7128 N, –74.0060 W)  
- Point 2: (34.0522 N, –118.2437 W)

Once I have those, I’ll compute the slope gradient in degrees for you.
message.reasoning: We need to calculate slope gradient between two points. But slope gradient requires elevation difference and horizontal distance. We only have lat/lon coordinates. Without elevation data, cannot compute slope. We can approximate horizontal distance using haversine formula. But slope gradient requires vertical difference. We don't have elevation. So we should explain that insufficient data. Possibly ask for elevations.
